```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
```

comdynamite simulates metacommunities with the process-based model of
Thompson et al. (2020). Each simulation has four ingredients:

1. a **landscape**: sites, their environment and how individuals disperse
   among them;
2. **species traits**: environmental optimum, niche breadth and maximum
   growth rate, with or without phylogenetic signal;
3. a **competition matrix**;
4. the **dispersal** rate.

```{r setup}
library(comdynamite)
set.seed(42)
```

## A first metacommunity

We draw a tree of 40 species, give their optima a strong phylogenetic signal
(Brownian motion, `lambda = 1`), and let close relatives compete more
strongly.

```{r}
tr <- ape::rcoal(40)
traits <- species_traits(tr, lambda = 1)
alpha <- competition_matrix(tr, type = "phylo", inter_max = 0.1)
land <- landscape_implicit(n_sites = 50)

sim <- simulate_metacommunity(land, traits, alpha, dispersal = 0.01, n_steps = 500)
sim
```

`sim$abundance` holds the abundance of each species at each site at the last
step. Ordering sites by their environment and species by their optimum shows
the sorting of species along the gradient:

```{r}
a <- sim$abundance[order(land$env), order(traits$optimum)]
image(log1p(a), xlab = "sites (by environment)", ylab = "species (by optimum)",
      axes = FALSE, col = hcl.colors(20, "YlGnBu", rev = TRUE))
```

## Species sorting and mass effects

Dispersal changes the regime. With low dispersal, species occur where the
environment suits them (species sorting); with high dispersal, they also occur
in unsuitable sites that are kept supplied by immigrants (mass effects), so
local richness increases and composition tracks the environment less closely.

```{r}
regimes <- c(sorting = 0.01, mass_effects = 0.5)
res <- lapply(regimes, function(d)
  simulate_metacommunity(land, traits, alpha, dispersal = d, n_steps = 500))
sapply(res, function(s) c(
  mean_richness = mean(rowSums(s$abundance > 0)),
  persisting = sum(colSums(s$abundance) > 0)
))
```

## Spatially explicit landscapes

`landscape_grid()` places sites on a grid, by default wrapped as a torus, with
a spatially autocorrelated environment and an exponential dispersal kernel.

```{r}
grid <- landscape_grid(side = 10, env_bandwidth = 2, disp_scale = 2)
image(matrix(grid$env, 10, 10), asp = 1, axes = FALSE,
      col = hcl.colors(20, "Earth"), main = "environment")
sim_sp <- simulate_metacommunity(grid, traits, alpha, dispersal = 0.1, n_steps = 500)
sim_sp
```

With spatial structure, sites are no longer exchangeable, so permuting sites
at random is not a valid null model. `torus_permutations()` gives the
rearrangements of a torus (translations and the eight symmetries of the
square) that keep all distances among sites, and therefore the spatial
autocorrelation of the environment:

```{r}
perms <- torus_permutations(10)
dim(perms)
# the environment under the first rearrangement
env_perm <- grid$env[perms[1, ]]
```

## An environment that changes over time

`env_over_time()` adds autocorrelated temporal fluctuations to the environment
of each site, and `record_steps` keeps abundances at chosen steps.

```{r}
et <- env_over_time(land$env, n_steps = 500, rho = 0.95, sd = 5)
sim_t <- simulate_metacommunity(land, traits, alpha, dispersal = 0.01, n_steps = 500,
                                env_time = et, record_steps = seq(100, 500, 100))
apply(sim_t$history > 0, 3, function(x) mean(rowSums(x)))
```

## Differences from Thompson et al. (2020)

The model follows the published equations. Two conventions differ:

* `sigma` is the standard deviation of the Gaussian response, so it equals
  `sqrt(2)` times the niche breadth parameter of Thompson et al. (2020);
* `alpha[j, k]` is the effect of species k on species j.

`env_over_time()` is a simple autoregressive generator, not the one used by
Thompson et al. (2020).

## Reference

Thompson, P. L., Guzman, L. M., De Meester, L., Horváth, Z., Ptacnik, R.,
Vanschoenwinkel, B., Viana, D. S., & Chase, J. M. (2020). A process-based
metacommunity framework linking local and regional scale community ecology.
*Ecology Letters*, 23, 1314–1329. https://doi.org/10.1111/ele.13568
